transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-16
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Atlas Head of ML), Ethan Morales (Atlas Backend), Liam O'Connor (Atlas SRE)

Summary (auto): quick run through of edge-case playbook for inference surge, focusing on operational mitigations for long-context applications and high-concurrency streaming.

00:00 [Maya]: hey everyone, thanks for carving the time, um we'll run through a short playbook and demo. Jonas and I will share console views and then run a simulated surge.
00:20 [Priya]: great, thanks. quick context — we're doing a customer support augmentation app, sessions keep long history per user, sometimes up to 30-50k tokens. traffic is spiky; peak qps around 2k for short windows.
00:35 [Jonas]: ok that helps. so our demo will show three failure modes: streaming backpressure under high tps, timeouts when kv cache can't be populated fast enough, and graceful fallback when model variants are incompatible.
01:02 [Ethan]: to be clear — we're leaning towards hosted first but dedicated is on the table if latency jitter is an issue or data isolation demands it.
01:15 [Maya]: totally. we'll run both scenarios. one note — some people call KV cache "K V" or "kv-cache" — our runtime stores prefix states so for long context we try to re-use keys rather than re-encode whole history.
01:40 [Liam]: are we talking prefix only or full attention state? we need to understand memory blow-up.
01:50 [Jonas]: good question — it's primarily prefix/KV snapshotting for the key-value attention cache; not full attention matrix. worst case, history eviction policy kicks in and we sketch a truncation strategy.
02:10 [Priya]: what about streaming? our frontend shows tokens to users in real-time and spikes cause the UI to hang if the stream stalls.
02:25 [Jonas]: streaming is continuous batches emitted as SSE or chunked responses. under surge you can hit backlog in the runtime's request queue, causing head-of-line blocking. our playbook suggests two paths: 1) heuristic shedding (drop non-critical sessions), 2) model variant fallback with lower compute.
02:50 [Ethan]: shed how? random? priority based?
03:05 [Maya]: priority based — we tag sessions with SLA level. we also recommend short time-to-first-token SLO and then background completion. so the UI gets a quick partial answer and the heavier summary completes async.
03:38 [Priya]: are there standard batching knobs we should tune? we've tried increasing batch size but saw latency increase.
03:50 [Jonas]: there are three levers: target_batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, and concurrency_per_gpu. increasing batch size reduces cost but can increase tail latency; aim for histogram-based configs — we can generate recommended defaults from your traffic sample.
04:20 [Liam]: what about timeouts? our infra retries aggressively which may amplify traffic.
04:35 [Maya]: yes retries can cascade. set idempotency tokens and client-side de-dupe, and tuning of client retry backoff is critical. on Redwood we also have server-side retry guards and request fingerprinting to drop duplicates.
05:00 [Jonas]: demo time — i'll share the Console. (screen share noises)
05:15 [Jonas]: here is model catalog, we pinned a v-quantized variant for the demo. notice the per-route policies — you can set fallback to a cheaper variant automatically when latency exceeds threshold.
06:00 [Priya]: that fallback — does it keep session continuity? or do we drop conversation context?
06:18 [Jonas]: it translates the session state where possible; sometimes you accept a short distilled summary if memory is incompatible. it's a lossy conversion but designed for availability.
06:36 [Ethan]: show us the streaming instrument? where can we see queue depth and per-token latency?
06:47 [Jonas]: metrics pane — token throughput, queue length, p95/p99 per-token lat. also trace links to the request id into our span trace. (he clicks) you can see the surge simulation toggle.
07:20 [Maya]: note — some product names may be mis-read by the transcription, like "Redwood Dedicated" becoming "red wood dedicated" — ignore small mis-reads.
07:38 [Jonas]: starting surge sim: baseline 200 qps, spike to 2200 qps for 30s, with 40k token sessions in 10% of requests. watch queue length and shed events.
08:02 [Priya]: ok watching the trace — i see a bunch of 504s in the initial run. why 504 not 429?
08:15 [Jonas]: 504 indicates gateway timeout on the client side; we configured server-side to return 429 for shedding but if the load passes an external LB the client may see 504. we recommend coordinated timeouts across infra components.
08:35 [Liam]: how do we maintain audit logs for sessions that were shed? compliance needs an audit record.
08:45 [Maya]: every request has an immutable audit event stored in the control plane with metadata: session id, reason for shed (policy id), fallback variant. we log minimal input if required for privacy; we can integrate KMS tags for encrypted artifacts.
09:10 [Ethan]: there are a few phrases in your docs referencing "compile-time kernels" — does that mean model kernels are recompiled for quantized variants on deploy?
09:25 [Jonas]: yes, the runtime selects optimized kernels at deploy and will recompile for some quantization paths. that can add a warm-up delay; we keep warm pools to mitigate that. for dedicated customers we pre-warm.
09:50 [Priya]: any SOC2/ISO stuff? our security team will demand the checklist.
10:00 [Maya]: we'll share the security FAQ and the SOC2 report excerpt; for private deployments we do KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed VPCs.
10:20 [Ethan]: demo showed fallback to a smaller model — how's quality measured?
10:28 [Jonas]: integrate our Optimize module — it runs eval sets and gives regression alerts; you pin quality gates per route. if fallback drops below gate, we can auto-notify and route to a human-in-the-loop.
10:50 [Priya]: interesting. could we do a canary where 5% goes to dedicated with dedicated GPU pool?
11:00 [Maya]: yes, Dedicated supports canaries and traffic split. we can provision a small reserved capacity for you to validate latency tail without impacting production.
11:18 [Ethan]: what's the rough delta on unit cost for dedicated vs hosted?
11:25 [Maya]: depends on utilization; dedicated has higher base but you get predictable throughput. we typically model per-token plus reserved minute amortization. we'll send an econ snapshot after we see your traffic profile.
11:55 [Priya]: back to streaming — if a session is long and the kv cache evicts, can you replay a compressed index or do we have to re-embed full history?
12:12 [Jonas]: we support partial re-embed: keep recent n-turns as dense vectors and summarize older context. sometimes mis-transcription calls this "history compaction". the tradeoff is latency vs fidelity.
12:40 [Liam]: logging/telemetry — can we ingest our own tracers or do we use your agents?
12:52 [Maya]: we expose tracing hooks and accept OTLP spans; you can forward traces to your observability backend and we surface token-level metrics in the Console.
13:10 [Ethan]: what's your recommended default for request timeout at edge? we typically do 30s.
13:20 [Jonas]: for long-contexts with streaming, aim for 60s end-to-end, but instrument time-to-first-token target of 500-800ms. longer tail can be backgrounded.
13:45 [Priya]: any tips for client retries to avoid amplification?
13:50 [Maya]: exponential backoff with jitter, and idempotency keys. also prefer circuit-breakers and client token bucket to smooth bursts.
14:12 [Jonas]: starting the second run — now with canary fallback enabled to cheaper model variant and background completion.
14:35 [Priya]: i see reduced 504s but more partial results. expected.
14:45 [Ethan]: can we surface user-visible reason codes instead of opaque errors so frontend can show a specific UI?
14:55 [Maya]: yes we return structured status codes and reason tags which you can map to UI text, e.g. "ShedByPolicy:priority_low" or "FallbackApplied:model_smaller".
15:10 [Liam]: question about KV eviction thresholds — can we configure per-customer?
15:20 [Jonas]: yes, per-tenant policies are available with Dedicated or Private; hosted has some tenant-level knobs but higher tiers unlock more control.
15:40 [Priya]: are there any quick wins for us to reduce cost without hurting latency?
15:48 [Maya]: a couple: 1) prefix-level caching on repetitive system prompts, 2) distilled summarization for older history, 3) adaptive batching tuned to your 95th percentile request size.
16:10 [Ethan]: ok next steps; we'll send sample traces and traffic histogram. can you run the bench?
16:20 [Maya]: yes we'll run bench with your sample under a short dedicated trial. Jonas will own the bench run.
16:30 [Priya]: any other blockers from infra? SSO and SAML are must-haves for us.
16:40 [Maya]: we support SAML SSO and can integrate with your IdP. we'll include var docs.
16:55 [Jonas]: quick note — some terminology may be garbled in the transcript: "KV cache" sometimes appears as "K V cash" and "Optimize" as "opt my eyes" in speech-to-text; just ignore that.
17:08 [Maya]: wrap-up: recap actions and timeline.
17:15 [Maya]: action list: share deck, run bench, exchange security artifacts, schedule follow-up. Thanks everyone, great session.
17:30 [Priya]: thanks — excited to see the bench results.
17:40 [Ethan]: thanks both.
17:45 [Liam]: bye.

Notes: transcript contains typical ASR glitches, some product names mis-spelled. Shared artifacts: surge-playbook deck (link above), security FAQ (will be attached).

End of transcript.
